blocks.text:
No cleanup of input folder in this repo — input folder cleanup is a dmtools runtime feature (`--cleanupInputFolder` param, default true per AGENTS.md hints: "Pass --cleanupInputFolder false so you can inspect input/<KEY>/ afterwards" — implying the DEFAULT is cleanup=true, i.e., the input folder is DELETED after the job completes by the dmtools runtime).

So: after each rework leg completes, dmtools deletes input/<ticketKey>/ (cleanupInputFolder defaults to true). The next leg's setup recreates it. Therefore a stale ci_violations.json does NOT survive into the next leg — the snapshot always reflects the CURRENT leg's setup-time CI state. Good — the staleness concern is mitigated by the runtime's input-folder lifecycle (outside this repo).

But wait — one more scenario within a single leg: reject → re-run leg. `handleOwnedViolationsRejected` → the leg fails → the rework runner re-runs (the machine re-queues). The next leg's setup re-detects CI (still red — violations not fixed) → rewrites ci_violations.json fresh. Consistent.

Edge: what if the leg is re-run WITHOUT setup (resume)? `resumeOrHandleInterrupted` path — input folder still present from the interrupted leg → snapshot still valid. Fine.

Now — the remaining deep-dive items:

1. Check `parseDiffPaths` edge: `---` lines from Markdown content in diffs. In a unified diff, a deleted Markdown line `--- heading` appears as `---- heading`?? No wait: a deleted line's content `--- heading` is rendered as `-` + `--- heading` = `---- heading`. Hmm no: `-` prefix + content `-- heading`? Let me redo: content line `--- foo` deleted → diff line `---- foo`? No — `-` + `--- foo` = `---- foo`. Right, 4 dashes. So `^--- ` (3 dashes + space) never matches deleted content lines... unless the content line is `-- foo` deleted → `--- foo` — MATCHES `^--- (.+)$` → adds `foo`... wait `-- foo` deleted renders as `--- foo` — that WOULD match the `--- a/(.+)` pattern: `^--- (?:(?:a\/)?(.+))$` — `m[1]` = `foo` (the `a/` optional prefix not present). So a deleted Markdown thematic break or a deleted line starting with `-- ` injects a bogus diff path `foo`. Also ADED line `++ foo` → `+++ foo` matches `^\+\+ (.+)$` → bogus path `foo`.

Impact: a bogus short path in the diff set could make an unrelated violation "owned" if sameFile matches. sameFile requires v === d or suffix match `/`+d — bogus path `foo` (2+ chars): a violation in `some/dir/foo` would suffix-match `foo` → owned. Rare but possible (Markdown docs edits with `-- ` lines...). How likely is a diff containing a changed line whose content starts with `++ ` or `-- `? Markdown thematic breaks are `---` → deleted renders `----` (no match); `--` is rare. Added line starting with `++ `: e.g. a diff of a diff, or Markdown `++emphasis++` (pandoc markup). Quite rare. It's a heuristic extractor; the failure mode is a slightly over-broad owned set (fail-safe direction: owned = must fix, not dismiss). I'll note as SUGESTION.

Actually more common: `index 000..abc` lines, `@@ -13,7 +13,8 @@` hunk headers — `@@` lines don't match. Context lines start with space. The `+++ b/...` real header — matched once, deduped.

Hmm — wait, actually one more real case: a PR diff that CONTAINS a diff (e.g. this very PR adds fixture files with diff content inside! `js/unit-tests/fixtures/ci_logs/diff_pr_433.txt` contains lines `diff --git a/test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart b/test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart` INSIDE the fixture — when ciViolations parses THIS PR's own diff, parseDiffPaths would add `test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart` as a "diff path" because the fixture text embeds a nested diff! For self-referential PRs (like this one), ownership tagging can be fooled by embedded diff text. Cute edge case — only affects PRs that embed diff text in changed files (fixtures, docs). Direction of error: could mark a violation owned that isn't (fail-closed, makes the leg fix it — safe direction) or foreign... it adds extra owned paths. Fail-safe direction again. SUGESTION.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Now let me review the key test files and check remaining diffs. Let me look at test_ciViolations.js, test_pushReworkChanges.js changes, test_preCliReworkSetup.js changes, test_githubHelpers.js changes, and the fixtures. Also let me check CI status of the PR head.

Potential issues to investigate in ciViolations.js:

1. `sameFile`: `v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d` — checks suffix match with a '/' separator. OK. But case sensitivity — paths compared case-sensitively; fine for git.

2. `addDiffTargetPath`: regex `^--- (?:(?:a\/)?(.+))$` — this also matches `--- a/...` and bare `--- path`. Hmm, but in a diff, the `---` line could also be a removed line starting with `---` (e.g. in a Markdown diff where a line `--- something` was deleted). That would add false diff paths. Minor. Actually in unified diffs, a deleted line begins with a single `-`, so a deleted line containing `--- foo` appears as `---- foo`. And a context line ` --- foo`. So `^--- ` only matches the file header. OK, fine. But wait — `+++ b/...` for added file — `^--- /dev/null` skipped. Good.

But there's a subtle issue: `addDiffHeaderPaths` matches `diff --git a/(.*) b/(.*)$` — with greedy `(.*)` for group 1. For a path containing ` b/` this could mis-split, but greedy regex: `^diff --git a\/(.*) b\/(.*)$` — group 1 greedy takes as much as possible while still allowing ` b/` and group 2. For `a/x b/y b/z` (rename with space in filename), group 1 = `x b/y`, group 2 = `z`. Edge case, rare. Not worth blocking.

3. `tagOwnership` — `v.path && diffPaths` — if `diffPaths` is `[]` (empty diff, e.g. empty string diff?), then `diffText ? parseDiffPaths(diffText) : null` — if diffText is non-empty but parses to zero paths, diffPaths = [] which is truthy → pathed violations → 'foreign'. Hmm — if the diff text is provided but unparseable (a different diff format), everything pathed becomes "foreign — do not chase", which is exactly the failure mode this PR tries to prevent. The degradation to `unknown` only happens when diffText is null/empty. A safer invariant: if `parseDiffPaths` yields zero paths, treat as no diff evidence → unknown. That's a legit IMPORTANT finding: `gitOps.getPRDiff` could return e.g. "Merge conflict" error text or empty string on failure. Let me check `getPRDiff` behavior.

4. `crap4jViolations`: `currentRule` set only on FAIL. If `[FAIL]` header line exists but detail lines not indented with `path:line` pattern — no violations. Degradation handled.

Note: detail regex `^\s*(.+?):(\d+):\s*(.+?)\s*$` — `.+?` non-gredy, matches `path` — but for Windows path `C:\repo\lib\x.dart:13: msg`, `(.+?):(\d+):` — non-gredy: first tries shortest `.` then `:(\d+):`. `C` then `:`? Next char is `\r` not digit. It would extend until `C:\repo\lib\x.dart` followed by `:13:`. Wait — but there's `:13:` — hmm, first colon-digit-colon match... `C:` — after `C` comes `:` then `\` — not a digit. Continue... eventually `x.dart:13:` — good. But note normalizePath is applied later in tagOwnership via sameFile. Good.

But one thing: in `crap4jViolations`, `detail[1]` path may be quoted or absolute; normalized in sameFile. OK.

5. `dartAnalyzeViolations` — regex requires `•` separators and `code` at end. Standard dart analyze format: ` error • The method 'build' isn't defined • lib/widgets/foo_widget.dart:12:7 • undefined_method`. Good. Severity `warning`/`info` become violations too — with `[warning]`/`[info]` prefix in detail. This could inflate the owned list with analyzer warnings that aren't gate failures (the check failed or not). Hmm — but the extractor only runs on logs of FAILED checks. For `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.` — `exit code 1.` — hmm: regex `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/\\]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+` — `code 1.` — token candidates: `code`? no dot. `1.` — `1.` needs `[A-Za-z0-9]+` after the dot — after `1.` is end/space → no. blocks.text:
No cleanup of input folder in this repo — input folder cleanup is a dmtools runtime feature (`--cleanupInputFolder` param, default true per AGENTS.md hints: "Pass --cleanupInputFolder false so you can inspect input/<KEY>/ afterwards" — implying the DEFAULT is cleanup=true, i.e., the input folder is DELETED after the job completes by the dmtools runtime).

So: after each rework leg completes, dmtools deletes input/<ticketKey>/ (cleanupInputFolder defaults to true). The next leg's setup recreates it. Therefore a stale ci_violations.json does NOT survive into the next leg — the snapshot always reflects the CURRENT leg's setup-time CI state. Good — the staleness concern is mitigated by the runtime's input-folder lifecycle (outside this repo).

But wait — one more scenario within a single leg: reject → re-run leg. `handleOwnedViolationsRejected` → the leg fails → the rework runner re-runs (the machine re-queues). The next leg's setup re-detects CI (still red — violations not fixed) → rewrites ci_violations.json fresh. Consistent.

Edge: what if the leg is re-run WITHOUT setup (resume)? `resumeOrHandleInterrupted` path — input folder still present from the interrupted leg → snapshot still valid. Fine.

1. Check `parseDiffPaths` edge: `---` lines from Markdown content in diffs. In a unified diff, a deleted Markdown line `--- heading` appears as `---- heading`?? {
  "key": "pr-1131",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1119 Rework context: extract gate violations (owned vs foreign) to the top of ci_failures.md forbid dismissing owned violations",
    "description": "Closes #1119
### What changed
Rework legs now receive every CI gate violation as a first-class list: a pure extractor (`js/common/ciViolations.js`) parses raw job logs (crap4dart, dart analyze, dart test, jscpd, `##[error]` fallback), tags each item `owned`/`foreign` against the PR diff, and `ci_failures.md` opens with **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** followed by "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)" — the 500-line tails and `ci_failures_full.log` stay below as evidence. The post-rework summary is mechanically validated: a summary dismissing an owned violation as "not caused by this PR"/"unrelated"/"infra" fails the leg and counts as an empty lap.

### Key decisions
- Context assembly, not model judgment: owned rows carry `check | rule | path:line | measured-vs-limit`; the full uncapped list lands in `ci_violations.json` (tables cap at 50 rows)
- Renames count as owned (old+new diff paths); Windows/`./` paths normalized; no diff evidence degrades to `unknown`, never "do not chase"
- Degradation invariant: unknown log shape → no table, `ci_failures.md` assembled exactly as today; raw logs are never dropped
- `preCliReworkSetup` fetches the PR diff **before** CI detection so ownership tagging has it; `preparePRForReview` passes the diff too
- Rejection path (`pushReworkChanges.runOwnedViolationsGate`) posts a per-item rejection comment with the owned table and an empty lap marker for the gh-957 no-op loop guard
- Prompt/instructions updated (`pr_rework_prompt.md`, `instructions/pr_rework/*`, `instructions/review/ci_failures.md`): owned violations must be listed per item with `fixed` / `disputed: <reason>`

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_ciViolations.json   # UT-1..UT-8, E1..E3
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 5015 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LOGS[Failed-check raw logs] --> EX[ciViolations.extractViolations]
  DIFF[pr_diff.txt file list] --> TAG[ciViolations.tagOwnership]
  EX --> TAG
  TAG --> MD["ci_failures.md: owned table → foreign list → raw tails"]
  TAG --> JSON[ci_violations.json uncapped]
  MD --> REWORK[Rework leg fixes owned rows]
  REWORK --> GATE[runOwnedViolationsGate: summary must account fixed/disputed per item]
  GATE -->|dismissal while owned open| FAIL[leg failed + empty lap marker]
  GATE -->|accounted| DONE[normal completion]
```

</details>"
  }
}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Now let me review the key test files and check remaining diffs. Let me look at test_ciViolations.js, test_pushReworkChanges.js changes, test_preCliReworkSetup.js changes, test_githubHelpers.js changes, and the fixtures. Also let me check CI status of the PR head.

Potential issues to investigate in ciViolations.js:

1. `sameFile`: `v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d` — checks suffix match with a '/' separator. OK. But case sensitivity — paths compared case-sensitively; fine for git.

2. `addDiffTargetPath`: regex `^--- (?:(?:a\/)?(.+))$` — this also matches `--- a/...` and bare `--- path`. Hmm, but in a diff, the `---` line could also be a removed line starting with `---` (e.g. in a Markdown diff where a line `--- something` was deleted). That would add false diff paths. Minor. Actually in unified diffs, a deleted line begins with a single `-`, so a deleted line containing `--- foo` appears as `---- foo`. And a context line ` --- foo`. So `^--- ` only matches the file header. OK, fine. But wait — `+++ b/...` for added file — `^--- /dev/null` skipped. Good.

But there's a subtle issue: `addDiffHeaderPaths` matches `diff --git a/(.*) b/(.*)$` — with greedy `(.*)` for group 1. For a path containing ` b/` this could mis-split, but greedy regex: `^diff --git a\/(.*) b\/(.*)$` — group 1 greedy takes as much as possible while still allowing ` b/` and group 2. For `a/x b/y b/z` (rename with space in filename), group 1 = `x b/y`, group 2 = `z`. Edge case, rare. Not worth blocking.

3. `tagOwnership` — `v.path && diffPaths` — if `diffPaths` is `[]` (empty diff, e.g. empty string diff?), then `diffText ? parseDiffPaths(diffText) : null` — if diffText is non-empty but parses to zero paths, diffPaths = [] which is truthy → pathed violations → 'foreign'. Hmm — if the diff text is provided but unparseable (a different diff format), everything pathed becomes "foreign — do not chase", which is exactly the failure mode this PR tries to prevent. The degradation to `unknown` only happens when diffText is null/empty. A safer invariant: if `parseDiffPaths` yields zero paths, treat as no diff evidence → unknown. That's a legit IMPORTANT finding: `gitOps.getPRDiff` could return e.g. "Merge conflict" error text or empty string on failure. Let me check `getPRDiff` behavior.

4. `crap4jViolations`: `currentRule` set only on FAIL. If `[FAIL]` header line exists but detail lines not indented with `path:line` pattern — no violations. Degradation handled.

Note: detail regex `^\s*(.+?):(\d+):\s*(.+?)\s*$` — `.+?` non-gredy, matches `path` — but for Windows path `C:\repo\lib\x.dart:13: msg`, `(.+?):(\d+):` — non-gredy: first tries shortest `.` then `:(\d+):`. `C` then `:`? Next char is `\r` not digit. It would extend until `C:\repo\lib\x.dart` followed by `:13:`. Wait — but there's `:13:` — hmm, first colon-digit-colon match... `C:` — after `C` comes `:` then `\` — not a digit. Continue... eventually `x.dart:13:` — good. But note normalizePath is applied later in tagOwnership via sameFile. Good.

But one thing: in `crap4jViolations`, `detail[1]` path may be quoted or absolute; normalized in sameFile. OK.

5. `dartAnalyzeViolations` — regex requires `•` separators and `code` at end. Standard dart analyze format: ` error • The method 'build' isn't defined • lib/widgets/foo_widget.dart:12:7 • undefined_method`. Good. Severity `warning`/`info` become violations too — with `[warning]`/`[info]` prefix in detail. This could inflate the owned list with analyzer warnings that aren't gate failures (the check failed or not). Hmm — but the extractor only runs on logs of FAILED checks. Analyzer warnings in a failed check's log are legitimately noise, and tagging them as "owned — must fix" could force rework legs to fix pre-existing warnings in files they touched. That's actually intended per the ticket (fix violations in changed files). OK.

6. `dartTestViolations` — matches `path: test name [E]`. OK.

No cleanup of input folder in this repo — input folder cleanup is a dmtools runtime feature (`--cleanupInputFolder` param, default true per AGENTS.md hints: "Pass --cleanupInputFolder false so you can inspect input/<KEY>/ afterwards" — implying the DEFAULT is cleanup=true, i.e., the input folder is DELETED after the job completes by the dmtools runtime).

So: after each rework leg completes, dmtools deletes input/<ticketKey>/ (cleanupInputFolder defaults to true). The next leg's setup recreates it. Therefore a stale ci_violations.json does NOT survive into the next leg — the snapshot always reflects the CURRENT leg's setup-time CI state. Good — the staleness concern is mitigated by the runtime's input-folder lifecycle (outside this repo).

But wait — one more scenario within a single leg: reject → re-run leg. `handleOwnedViolationsRejected` → the leg fails → the rework runner re-runs (the machine re-queues). The next leg's setup re-detects CI (still red — violations not fixed) → rewrites ci_violations.json fresh. Consistent.

Edge: what if the leg is re-run WITHOUT setup (resume)? `resumeOrHandleInterrupted` path — input folder still present from the interrupted leg → snapshot still valid. Fine.

Now — the remaining deep-dive items:

1. Check `parseDiffPaths` edge: `---` lines from Markdown content in diffs. In a unified diff, a deleted Markdown line `--- heading` appears as `---- heading`?? No wait: a deleted line's content `--- heading` is rendered as `-` + `--- heading` = `---- heading`. Hmm no: `-` prefix + content `-- heading`? Let me redo: content line `--- foo` deleted → diff line `---- foo`? No — `-` + `--- foo` = `---- foo`. Right, 4 dashes. So `^--- ` (3 dashes + space) never matches deleted content lines... unless the content line is `-- foo` deleted → `--- foo` — MATCHES `^--- (.+)$` → adds `foo`... wait `-- foo` deleted renders as `--- foo` — that WOULD match the `--- a/(.+)` pattern: `^--- (?:(?:a\/)?(.+))$` — `m[1]` = `foo` (the `a/` optional prefix not present). So a deleted Markdown thematic break or a deleted line starting with `-- ` injects a bogus diff path `foo`. Also ADED line `++ foo` → `+++ foo` matches `^\+\+ (.+)$` → bogus path `foo`.

Impact: a bogus short path in the diff set could make an unrelated violation "owned" if sameFile matches. sameFile requires v === d or suffix match `/`+d — bogus path `foo` (2+ chars): a violation in `some/dir/foo` would suffix-match `foo` → owned. Rare but possible (Markdown docs edits with `-- ` lines...). How likely is a diff containing a changed line whose content starts with `++ ` or `-- `? Markdown thematic breaks are `---` → deleted renders `----` (no match); `--` is rare. Added line starting with `++ `: e.g. a diff of a diff, or Markdown `++emphasis++` (pandoc markup). Quite rare. It's a heuristic extractor; the failure mode is a slightly over-broad owned set (fail-safe direction: owned = must fix, not dismiss). I'll note as SUGESTION.

Actually more common: `index 000..abc` lines, `@@ -13,7 +13,8 @@` hunk headers — `@@` lines don't match. Context lines start with space. The `+++ b/...` real header — matched once, deduped.

Hmm — wait, actually one more real case: a PR diff that CONTAINS a diff (e.g. this very PR adds fixture files with diff content inside! `js/unit-tests/fixtures/ci_logs/diff_pr_433.txt` contains lines `diff --git a/test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart b/test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart` INSIDE the fixture — when ciViolations parses THIS PR's own diff, parseDiffPaths would add `test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart` as a "diff path" because the fixture text embeds a nested diff! For self-referential PRs (like this one), ownership tagging can be fooled by embedded diff text. Cute edge case — only affects PRs that embed diff text in changed files (fixtures, docs). Direction of error: could mark a violation owned that isn't (fail-closed, makes the leg fix it — safe direction) or foreign... it adds extra owned paths. Fail-safe direction again. SUGESTION.

content.text:
Rework context: extract gate violations (owned vs foreign) to the top of ci_failures.md; forbid dismissing owned violations
## Goal — rework legs see the exact gate violations they must fix (v1)
One sentence: **when a quality gate is red, the rework leg receives every violation line (file:line, rule, measured vs limit) as a first-class, top-of-file list, so that it fixes them instead of declaring the red "not caused by this PR".**

Live: epam/dmtools-dart#433 (gh-409), rework leg run 39308030238 at 2026-10-19 19:05.
- `gate` (crap4dart) failed with:
  ```
  [FAIL] method_size: 1 violations in 5903 methods over their size limits
    test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart:13: main has 100 lines > max 60
  ```
- The file was **added by this PR**. The violation line was present in `ci_failures_full.log`, and inside the last 500 lines of `ci_failures.md`.
- The agent's own grep (`method_size\|> *[0-9]* lines`) matched only the `[FAIL]` header and missed the indented detail line. It concluded *"none of my files exceeds 60 lines… violation is in code the PR does not touch"* and pushed `e20e9665` without fixing it. Its commit even grew the same `main` (+30 lines).
- In the same run a genuinely unrelated red, `agents-gate` (planned-file partition race on agents@main, a dmtools-dart workflow issue), was mixed in. The agent then classified **both** reds as "infra".

## Why this framing
- The fix is not "a smarter model". Context assembly must make violations impossible to miss and must separate PR-owned reds from foreign ones.
- Retracted: the context was missing. It was present but buried: 686-line raw logs × 5 checks, with no structure.

## Architecture
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], assembled by `js/common/githubHelpers.js` (`fetchAndWriteCiFailures` / `buildLogSections`) and `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`.

1. **Violation extractor** (pure function, `js/common/ciViolations.js`), given raw job logs, returns `[{check, rule, path, line, detail}]`. Recognized shapes:
   - crap4dart/crap4j: `[FAIL] <rule>:` header + indented `path:line: …` lines until the next `[PASS|FAIL|WARN]`.
   - dart analyze: `error • … • path:line:col • code`.
   - dart test: `path: <test name> [E]` / `Some tests failed`.
   - jscpd duplication blocks.
   - Generic `##[error]` lines (fallback).
2. **Ownership tag** per violation: `owned` when `path` is in the PR diff (`pr_diff.txt` file list), `foreign` otherwise, and `unknown` when there is no path.
3. `ci_failures.md` starts with a section **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"**, a table of `owned` items. Then "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)". The 500-line tails stay below as evidence.
4. The rework prompt rule is to check `ci_failures.md`: *an owned violation may not be dismissed as unrelated. Fix it or explain, per item, why the gate is wrong.*
5. The post-rework summary must list each owned violation with `fixed` / `disputed: <reason>`. A summary that claims "not caused by this PR" while owned items exist is rejected (the leg is marked failed, and the no-op loop guard counts it).

Invariants:
- I1 — extraction never drops the raw logs. The full log is still written (gh-1045).
- I2 — the extractor is deterministic and covered by unit tests with real log fixtures.
- I3 — an unknown log shape degrades to today's behavior, never to an empty file.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — the #433 gate log fixture yields exactly one owned violation `test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart:13 method_size main 100>60` (UT-1).
- **AC2** — the #433 agents-gate log yields one `foreign` item (`js/unit-tests/test_recoverDirtyReviewTestCase.js`, not in the diff) (UT-2).
- **AC3** — `ci_failures.md` opens with the owned table, followed by the foreign list (UT-3, snapshot).
- **AC4** — the fixtures for dart analyze, dart test, crap4j and jscpd each produce correct items (UT-4..7).
- **AC5** — unknown shape → no table, the 500-line tail stays as today (REG-1).
- **AC6** — the rework prompt contains the owned-violation rule. A summary validator rejects "unrelated" with owned items open (UT-8).
- **AC7** — replay #433: the rework leg input contains the owned row (IT-1).

## Test plan
`UT` in `js/unit-tests` with fixtures copied from dart run 39301703682 jobs 118246938987 (gate) and 118249670863 (agents-gate). `IT` via the preCliReworkSetup harness. `REG`: existing gh-1045 tests stay green.

### Edge cases
- E1 — violation in a file renamed by the PR → owned (match both old and new paths).
- E2 — more than 50 violations → table capped at 50 with a count, full list in `ci_violations.json`.
- E3 — Windows paths / `./` prefixes are normalized.

## Non-goals
- Fixing the agents-gate race itself (dmtools-dart workflow, separate issue).
- Changing the gate limits.

## References
epam/dmtools-dart#433, rework run 39308030238, Quality run 39301703682; gh-1045.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Now let me review the key test files and check remaining diffs. Let me look at test_ciViolations.js, test_pushReworkChanges.js changes, test_preCliReworkSetup.js changes, test_githubHelpers.js changes, and the fixtures. Also let me check CI status of the PR head.

Tests look thorough. Let me now check the fixtures and the remaining test diffs, plus the preCliReworkSetup test and preparePRForReview test. Also, check the CI status of this PR. Then do a careful review of the main module for bugs.

Potential issues to investigate in ciViolations.js:

1. `sameFile`: `v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d` — checks suffix match with a '/' separator. OK. But case sensitivity — paths compared case-sensitively; fine for git.

2. `addDiffTargetPath`: regex `^--- (?:(?:a\/)?(.+))$` — this also matches `--- a/...` and bare `--- path`. Hmm, but in a diff, the `---` line could also be a removed line starting with `---` (e.g. in a Markdown diff where a line `--- something` was deleted). That would add false diff paths. Minor. Actually in unified diffs, a deleted line begins with a single `-`, so a deleted line containing `--- foo` appears as `---- foo`. And a context line ` --- foo`. So `^--- ` only matches the file header. OK, fine. But wait — `+++ b/...` for added file — `^--- /dev/null` skipped. Good.

But there's a subtle issue: `addDiffHeaderPaths` matches `diff --git a/(.*) b/(.*)$` — with greedy `(.*)` for group 1. For a path containing ` b/` this could mis-split, but greedy regex: `^diff --git a\/(.*) b\/(.*)$` — group 1 greedy takes as much as possible while still allowing ` b/` and group 2. For `a/x b/y b/z` (rename with space in filename), group 1 = `x b/y`, group 2 = `z`. Edge case, rare. Not worth blocking.

3. `tagOwnership` — `v.path && diffPaths` — if `diffPaths` is `[]` (empty diff, e.g. empty string diff?), then `diffText ? parseDiffPaths(diffText) : null` — if diffText is non-empty but parses to zero paths, diffPaths = [] which is truthy → pathed violations → 'foreign'. Hmm — if the diff text is provided but unparseable (a different diff format), everything pathed becomes "foreign — do not chase", which is exactly the failure mode this PR tries to prevent. The degradation to `unknown` only happens when diffText is null/empty. A safer invariant: if `parseDiffPaths` yields zero paths, treat as no diff evidence → unknown. That's a legit IMPORTANT finding: `gitOps.getPRDiff` could return e.g. "Merge conflict" error text or empty string on failure. Let me check `getPRDiff` behavior.

4. `crap4jViolations`: `currentRule` set only on FAIL. If `[FAIL]` header line exists but detail lines not indented with `path:line` pattern — no violations. Degradation handled.

Note: detail regex `^\s*(.+?):(\d+):\s*(.+?)\s*$` — `.+?` non-gredy, matches `path` — but for Windows path `C:\repo\lib\x.dart:13: msg`, `(.+?):(\d+):` — non-gredy: first tries shortest `.` then `:(\d+):`. `C` then `:`? Next char is `\r` not digit. It would extend until `C:\repo\lib\x.dart` followed by `:13:`. Wait — but there's `:13:` — hmm, first colon-digit-colon match... `C:` — after `C` comes `:` then `\` — not a digit. Continue... eventually `x.dart:13:` — good. But note normalizePath is applied later in tagOwnership via sameFile. Good.

But one thing: in `crap4jViolations`, `detail[1]` path may be quoted or absolute; normalized in sameFile. OK.

5. `dartAnalyzeViolations` — regex requires `•` separators and `code` at end. Standard dart analyze format: ` error • The method 'build' isn't defined • lib/widgets/foo_widget.dart:12:7 • undefined_method`. Good. Severity `warning`/`info` become violations too — with `[warning]`/`[info]` prefix in detail. This could inflate the owned list with analyzer warnings that aren't gate failures (the check failed or not). Hmm — but the extractor only runs on logs of FAILED checks. Analyzer warnings in a failed check's log are legitimately noise, and tagging them as "owned — must fix" could force rework legs to fix pre-existing warnings in files they touched. That's actually intended per the ticket (fix violations in changed files). OK.

6. `dartTestViolations` — matches `path: test name [E]`. OK.

7. `jscpdViolations`: state machine with `taken` interplay. Note the interplay: `crap4jViolations` runs first and marks lines `taken`. jscpd's `Clone found` block entries ` path: 10-20` — the crap4j detail regex `^\s*(.+?):(\d+):\s*(.+?)\s*$` requires a third `:` — ` lib/x.dart: 10-20` has only one colon → not matched by crap4j. OK.

But there's a subtle bug in `jscpdViolations`: when `taken[idx]` is true (consumed by earlier parser) it resets `inBlock = false; blockEntries = []` — so a "Clone found" header followed by an already-taken entry line would flush early. Fine.

8. `findPathToken` — first path-like token. For `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.` — `exit code 1.` — hmm: regex `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/\\]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+` — `code 1.` — token candidates: `code`? no dot. `1.` — `1.` needs `[A-Za-z0-9]+` after the dot — after `1.` is end/space → no. Actually wait: `Process completed with exit code 1.` — is there any `x.y` pattern? No → null → pathless. Good, test covers it.

For a message like `##[error]NPM failed: see log at https://...` — URLs stripped first. Good.

But findPathToken could false-positive on e.g. `version 1.2.3 of tool` — token `1.2.3`? Match: `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/\\]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+` — leftmost: `1.2` (class matches `1`, dot, then `2`), token = [REDACTED:Sensitive Value], no separator → returns null (since indexOf('/') is -1). Good fallback to null.

Hmm wait — `var token = [REDACTED:Sensitive Value]]` is `m[0]`, and returns null if no separator. So `version.x` etc. won't produce paths. But a message like `Command failed: node scripts/x.js` → token `node` — wait, leftmost match: `node scripts/x.js` — the regex class doesn't include space, so leftmost match is... `node` has no dot. First dot-containing token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] → contains `/` → returned. 

9. `ghErrorViolation` — regex `/^.*##\[error\]\s?(.*?)\s*$/` — lazy match to end. Fine.

10. `errorAnnotationViolation` — `::error\s+([^:]*)::(.*?)\s*$` — `[^:]*` — but `file=...,line=...` may contain `::`? Fine. Note `file=` value could be URL-encoded. Minor.

11. `extractViolations` dedupe key: `rule|path|line|detail` — omits `check`. Two checks with same violation... they're extracted per check (extractViolations per checkName), so fine.

12. `buildViolationsMarkdown` — if only unknown items: returns just the note. If zero items total: ''. Good.

13. `violationsSummaryJson` — `new Date().toISOString()` in GralJS — should work. Wrapped in try. OK.

14. `validateOwnedViolationsSummary` — `mentionsViolation` uses `v.path` — if `v.path` is null (owned violations always have path since ownership owned requires path). Actually owned requires v.path truthy and diffPaths. OK. `normalizePath(v.path)` fine.

`violationAccounted` — checks per-line: line must contain path/basename/rule (lowercased) AND `fixed` or `disputed:`. Note `cariesAccountingMarker` also matches the bare word "fixed" anywhere — e.g. "The workflow is now fixed" + mentioning the path counts as accounting. False positives possible but acceptable design.

One issue: `mentionsViolation` — `basename.length > 3` — for basename like `a.dart` (6) fine. For rule matching: `normalizedLine.indexOf(String(v.rule).toLowerCase())` — rule `test` — any line containing the word "test" + "fixed" counts as accounting for the dart-test violation. With multiple owned violations in different files, a summary line "fixed all failing tests in foo_test.dart" would account for... the one whose path/basename matches. But a rule like `test` (dart test rule) means ANY line with "test" and "fixed" accounts for it. E.g. 3 owned violations: a.dart (rule method_size), b.dart (rule method_size), c_test.dart (rule test). Line "- fixed: a.dart" accounts for a.dart. The rule-`test` one needs a line with "test"+"fixed" — "- fixed: b.dart and rewrote the test" would falsely account for c_test.dart. Weak matching is a heuristic — acceptable, arguably by design ("names the violation"). SUGESTION level at most.

No cleanup of input folder in this repo — input folder cleanup is a dmtools runtime feature (`--cleanupInputFolder` param, default true per AGENTS.md hints: "Pass --cleanupInputFolder false so you can inspect input/<KEY>/ afterwards" — implying the DEFAULT is cleanup=true, i.e., the input folder is DELETED after the job completes by the dmtools runtime).

So: after each rework leg completes, dmtools deletes input/<ticketKey>/ (cleanupInputFolder defaults to true). The next leg's setup recreates it. Therefore a stale ci_violations.json does NOT survive into the next leg — the snapshot always reflects the CURRENT leg's setup-time CI state. Good — the staleness concern is mitigated by the runtime's input-folder lifecycle (outside this repo).

But wait — one more scenario within a single leg: reject → re-run leg. `handleOwnedViolationsRejected` → the leg fails → the rework runner re-runs (the machine re-queues). The next leg's setup re-detects CI (still red — violations not fixed) → rewrites ci_violations.json fresh. Consistent.

Edge: what if the leg is re-run WITHOUT setup (resume)? `resumeOrHandleInterrupted` path — input folder still present from the interrupted leg → snapshot still valid. Fine.

Now — the remaining deep-dive items:

1. Check `parseDiffPaths` edge: `---` lines from Markdown content in diffs. In a unified diff, a deleted Markdown line `--- heading` appears as `---- heading`?? No wait: a deleted line's content `--- heading` is rendered as `-` + `--- heading` = `---- heading`. Hmm no: `-` prefix + content `-- heading`? Let me redo: content line `--- foo` deleted → diff line `---- foo`? No — `-` + `--- foo` = `---- foo`. Right, 4 dashes. So `^--- ` (3 dashes + space) never matches deleted content lines... unless the content line is `-- foo` deleted → `--- foo` — MATCHES `^--- (.+)$` → adds `foo`... wait `-- foo` deleted renders as `--- foo` — that WOULD match the `--- a/(.+)` pattern: `^--- (?:(?:a\/)?(.+))$` — `m[1]` = `foo` (the `a/` optional prefix not present). So a deleted Markdown thematic break or a deleted line starting with `-- ` injects a bogus diff path `foo`. Also ADED line `++ foo` → `+++ foo` matches `^\+\+ (.+)$` → bogus path `foo`.

Impact: a bogus short path in the diff set could make an unrelated violation "owned" if sameFile matches. sameFile requires v === d or suffix match `/`+d — bogus path `foo` (2+ chars): a violation in `some/dir/foo` would suffix-match `foo` → owned. Rare but possible (Markdown docs edits with `-- ` lines...). How likely is a diff containing a changed line whose content starts with `++ ` or `-- `? Markdown thematic breaks are `---` → deleted renders `----` (no match); `--` is rare. Added line starting with `++ `: e.g. a diff of a diff, or Markdown `++emphasis++` (pandoc markup). Quite rare. It's a heuristic extractor; the failure mode is a slightly over-broad owned set (fail-safe direction: owned = must fix, not dismiss). I'll note as SUGESTION.

Actually more common: `index 000..abc` lines, `@@ -13,7 +13,8 @@` hunk headers — `@@` lines don't match. Context lines start with space. The `+++ b/...` real header — matched once, deduped.

Hmm — wait, actually one more real case: a PR diff that CONTAINS a diff (e.g. this very PR adds fixture files with diff content inside! `js/unit-tests/fixtures/ci_logs/diff_pr_433.txt` contains lines `diff --git a/test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart b/test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart` INSIDE the fixture — when ciViolations parses THIS PR's own diff, parseDiffPaths would add `test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart` as a "diff path" because the fixture text embeds a nested diff! For self-referential PRs (like this one), ownership tagging can be fooled by embedded diff text. Cute edge case — only affects PRs that embed diff text in changed files (fixtures, docs). Direction of error: could mark a violation owned that isn't (fail-closed, makes the leg fix it — safe direction) or foreign... it adds extra owned paths. Fail-safe direction again. SUGESTION.

2. Now check `detectFailedChecks` — is it also called from OTHER call sites that now need the diff? Let me grep for detectFailedChecks callers to see if any call site was missed (e.g. merge_finalize or other agents).

Rework context: extract gate violations (owned vs foreign) to the top of ci_failures.md; forbid dismissing owned violations
## Goal — rework legs see the exact gate violations they must fix (v1)
One sentence: **when a quality gate is red, the rework leg receives every violation line (file:line, rule, measured vs limit) as a first-class, top-of-file list, so that it fixes them instead of declaring the red "not caused by this PR".**

Live: epam/dmtools-dart#433 (gh-409), rework leg run 39308030238 at 2026-10-19 19:05.
- `gate` (crap4dart) failed with:
  ```
  [FAIL] method_size: 1 violations in 5903 methods over their size limits
    test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart:13: main has 100 lines > max 60
  ```
- The file was **added by this PR**. The violation line was present in `ci_failures_full.log`, and inside the last 500 lines of `ci_failures.md`.
- The agent's own grep (`method_size\|> *[0-9]* lines`) matched only the `[FAIL]` header and missed the indented detail line. It concluded *"none of my files exceeds 60 lines… violation is in code the PR does not touch"* and pushed `e20e9665` without fixing it. Its commit even grew the same `main` (+30 lines).
- In the same run a genuinely unrelated red, `agents-gate` (planned-file partition race on agents@main, a dmtools-dart workflow issue), was mixed in. The agent then classified **both** reds as "infra".

## Why this framing
- The fix is not "a smarter model". Context assembly must make violations impossible to miss and must separate PR-owned reds from foreign ones.
- Retracted: the context was missing. It was present but buried: 686-line raw logs × 5 checks, with no structure.

## Architecture
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], assembled by `js/common/githubHelpers.js` (`fetchAndWriteCiFailures` / `buildLogSections`) and `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`.

1. **Violation extractor** (pure function, `js/common/ciViolations.js`), given raw job logs, returns `[{check, rule, path, line, detail}]`. Recognized shapes:
   - crap4dart/crap4j: `[FAIL] <rule>:` header + indented `path:line: …` lines until the next `[PASS|FAIL|WARN]`.
   - dart analyze: `error • … • path:line:col • code`.
   - dart test: `path: <test name> [E]` / `Some tests failed`.
   - jscpd duplication blocks.
   - Generic `##[error]` lines (fallback).
2. **Ownership tag** per violation: `owned` when `path` is in the PR diff (`pr_diff.txt` file list), `foreign` otherwise, and `unknown` when there is no path.
3. `ci_failures.md` starts with a section **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"**, a table of `owned` items. Then "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)". The 500-line tails stay below as evidence.
4. The rework prompt rule is to check `ci_failures.md`: *an owned violation may not be dismissed as unrelated. Fix it or explain, per item, why the gate is wrong.*
5. The post-rework summary must list each owned violation with `fixed` / `disputed: <reason>`. A summary that claims "not caused by this PR" while owned items exist is rejected (the leg is marked failed, and the no-op loop guard counts it).

Invariants:
- I1 — extraction never drops the raw logs. The full log is still written (gh-1045).
- I2 — the extractor is deterministic and covered by unit tests with real log fixtures.
- I3 — an unknown log shape degrades to today's behavior, never to an empty file.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — the #433 gate log fixture yields exactly one owned violation `test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart:13 method_size main 100>60` (UT-1).
- **AC2** — the #433 agents-gate log yields one `foreign` item (`js/unit-tests/test_recoverDirtyReviewTestCase.js`, not in the diff) (UT-2).
- **AC3** — `ci_failures.md` opens with the owned table, followed by the foreign list (UT-3, snapshot).
- **AC4** — the fixtures for dart analyze, dart test, crap4j and jscpd each produce correct items (UT-4..7).
- **AC5** — unknown shape → no table, the 500-line tail stays as today (REG-1).
- **AC6** — the rework prompt contains the owned-violation rule. A summary validator rejects "unrelated" with owned items open (UT-8).
- **AC7** — replay #433: the rework leg input contains the owned row (IT-1).

## Test plan
`UT` in `js/unit-tests` with fixtures copied from dart run 39301703682 jobs 118246938987 (gate) and 118249670863 (agents-gate). `IT` via the preCliReworkSetup harness. `REG`: existing gh-1045 tests stay green.

### Edge cases
- E1 — violation in a file renamed by the PR → owned (match both old and new paths).
- E2 — more than 50 violations → table capped at 50 with a count, full list in `ci_violations.json`.
- E3 — Windows paths / `./` prefixes are normalized.

## Non-goals
- Fixing the agents-gate race itself (dmtools-dart workflow, separate issue).
- Changing the gate limits.

epam/dmtools-dart#433, rework run 39308030238, Quality run 39301703682; gh-1045.

The leg fails, empty lap counted, machine re-runs — wasted CI round, and the model gets a rejection comment listing errors including the dismissal claim. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Now let me review the key test files and check remaining diffs. Let me look at test_ciViolations.js, test_pushReworkChanges.js changes, test_preCliReworkSetup.js changes, test_githubHelpers.js changes, and the fixtures. Also let me check CI status of the PR head.

Tests look thorough. Let me now check the fixtures and the remaining test diffs, plus the preCliReworkSetup test and preparePRForReview test. Also, check the CI status of this PR. Then do a careful review of the main module for bugs.

Potential issues to investigate in ciViolations.js:

1. `sameFile`: `v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d` — checks suffix match with a '/' separator. OK. But case sensitivity — paths compared case-sensitively; fine for git.

2. `addDiffTargetPath`: regex `^--- (?:(?:a\/)?(.+))$` — this also matches `--- a/...` and bare `--- path`. Hmm, but in a diff, the `---` line could also be a removed line starting with `---` (e.g. in a Markdown diff where a line `--- something` was deleted). That would add false diff paths. Minor. Actually in unified diffs, a deleted line begins with a single `-`, so a deleted line containing `--- foo` appears as `---- foo`. And a context line ` --- foo`. So `^--- ` only matches the file header. OK, fine. But wait — `+++ b/...` for added file — `^--- /dev/null` skipped. Good.

But there's a subtle issue: `addDiffHeaderPaths` matches `diff --git a/(.*) b/(.*)$` — with greedy `(.*)` for group 1. For a path containing ` b/` this could mis-split, but greedy regex: `^diff --git a\/(.*) b\/(.*)$` — group 1 greedy takes as much as possible while still allowing ` b/` and group 2. For `a/x b/y b/z` (rename with space in filename), group 1 = `x b/y`, group 2 = `z`. Edge case, rare. Not worth blocking.

3. `tagOwnership` — `v.path && diffPaths` — if `diffPaths` is `[]` (empty diff, e.g. empty string diff?), then `diffText ? parseDiffPaths(diffText) : null` — if diffText is non-empty but parses to zero paths, diffPaths = [] which is truthy → pathed violations → 'foreign'. Hmm — if the diff text is provided but unparseable (a different diff format), everything pathed becomes "foreign — do not chase", which is exactly the failure mode this PR tries to prevent. The degradation to `unknown` only happens when diffText is null/empty. A safer invariant: if `parseDiffPaths` yields zero paths, treat as no diff evidence → unknown. That's a legit IMPORTANT finding: `gitOps.getPRDiff` could return e.g. "Merge conflict" error text or empty string on failure. Let me check `getPRDiff` behavior.

4. `crap4jViolations`: `currentRule` set only on FAIL. If `[FAIL]` header line exists but detail lines not indented with `path:line` pattern — no violations. Degradation handled.

Note: detail regex `^\s*(.+?):(\d+):\s*(.+?)\s*$` — `.+?` non-gredy, matches `path` — but for Windows path `C:\repo\lib\x.dart:13: msg`, `(.+?):(\d+):` — non-gredy: first tries shortest `.` then `:(\d+):`. `C` then `:`? Next char is `\r` not digit. It would extend until `C:\repo\lib\x.dart` followed by `:13:`. Wait — but there's `:13:` — hmm, first colon-digit-colon match... `C:` — after `C` comes `:` then `\` — not a digit. Continue... eventually `x.dart:13:` — good. But note normalizePath is applied later in tagOwnership via sameFile. Good.

But one thing: in `crap4jViolations`, `detail[1]` path may be quoted or absolute; normalized in sameFile. OK.

5. `dartAnalyzeViolations` — regex requires `•` separators and `code` at end. Standard dart analyze format: ` error • The method 'build' isn't defined • lib/widgets/foo_widget.dart:12:7 • undefined_method`. Good. Severity `warning`/`info` become violations too — with `[warning]`/`[info]` prefix in detail. This could inflate the owned list with analyzer warnings that aren't gate failures (the check failed or not). Hmm — but the extractor only runs on logs of FAILED checks. Analyzer warnings in a failed check's log are legitimately noise, and tagging them as "owned — must fix" could force rework legs to fix pre-existing warnings in files they touched. That's actually intended per the ticket (fix violations in changed files). OK.

Note the interplay: `crap4jViolations` runs first and marks lines `taken`. jscpd's `Clone found` block entries ` path: 10-20` — the crap4j detail regex `^\s*(.+?):(\d+):\s*(.+?)\s*$` requires a third `:` — ` lib/x.dart: 10-20` has only one colon → not matched by crap4j.
