epam/dmtools-dart#433, rework run 39308030238, Quality run 39301703682; gh-1045.

- **PR #**: 1131
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1131
- **Title**: gh-1119 Rework context: extract gate violations (owned vs foreign) to the top of ci_failures.md forbid dismissing owned violations
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1119` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 29
- **Additions**: +2086
- **Deletions**: -36
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T21:45:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T01:32:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1119
### What changed
Rework legs now receive every CI gate violation as a first-class list: a pure extractor (`js/common/ciViolations.js`) parses raw job logs (crap4dart, dart analyze, dart test, jscpd, `##[error]` fallback), tags each item `owned`/`foreign` against the PR diff, and `ci_failures.md` opens with **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** followed by "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)" — the 500-line tails and `ci_failures_full.log` stay below as evidence. The post-rework summary is mechanically validated: a summary dismissing an owned violation as "not caused by this PR"/"unrelated"/"infra" fails the leg and counts as an empty lap.

### Key decisions
- Context assembly, not model judgment: owned rows carry `check | rule | path:line | measured-vs-limit`; the full uncapped list lands in `ci_violations.json` (tables cap at 50 rows)
- Renames count as owned (old+new diff paths); Windows/`./` paths normalized; no diff evidence degrades to `unknown`, never "do not chase"
- Degradation invariant: unknown log shape → no table, `ci_failures.md` assembled exactly as today; raw logs are never dropped
- `preCliReworkSetup` fetches the PR diff **before** CI detection so ownership tagging has it; `preparePRForReview` passes the diff too
- Rejection path (`pushReworkChanges.runOwnedViolationsGate`) posts a per-item rejection comment with the owned table and an empty lap marker for the gh-957 no-op loop guard
- Prompt/instructions updated (`pr_rework_prompt.md`, `instructions/pr_rework/*`, `instructions/review/ci_failures.md`): owned violations must be listed per item with `fixed` / `disputed: <reason>`

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_ciViolations.json   # UT-1..UT-8, E1..E3
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 5015 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LOGS[Failed-check raw logs] --> EX[ciViolations.extractViolations]
  DIFF[pr_diff.txt file list] --> TAG[ciViolations.tagOwnership]
  EX --> TAG
  TAG --> MD["ci_failures.md: owned table → foreign list → raw tails"]
  TAG --> JSON[ci_violations.json uncapped]
  MD --> REWORK[Rework leg fixes owned rows]
  REWORK --> GATE[runOwnedViolationsGate: summary must account fixed/disputed per item]
  GATE -->|dismissal while owned open| FAIL[leg failed + empty lap marker]
  GATE -->|accounted| DONE[normal completion]
```

</details>

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: residual parser-order contamination — a path-bearing `##[error]path:line:` line inside an unterminated `[FAIL]` section is still swallowed with a mangled path and rendered as "foreign, do not chase"**

The reorder in `extractViolations` (this head) fully fixes the reported dart-analyze/dart-test contamination — I verified the `gate_plus_analyze.log` repro now extracts the bullet with its clean path and tags it `owned` (control check below). One narrower shape of the same family remains: `genericErrorViolations` runs **last**, so a `##[error]` line whose message carries `path:line:` and that appears **after a `[FAIL] <rule>:` header with no intervening `[PASS]/[WARN]/[FAIL]` marker** is claimed by `crap4jViolations` first.

Reproduced against this branch's module (`js/common/ciViolations.js`):

```js
extractViolations(
  '[FAIL] method_size: 1 violations\n' +
  ' a/one.dart:1: too big\n' +
  '##[error]lib/widgets/foo.dart:12: build failed', 'gate')

//   { rule:'method_size', path:'a/one.dart', line:1 },                              // correct
//   { rule:'method_size', path:'##[error]lib/widgets/foo.dart', line:12, ... }      // mangled
// ]
```

The mangled path (`##[error]` prefix baked into the captured "path") fails the `sameFile` suffix check even when `lib/widgets/foo.dart` IS in the diff, so a genuinely owned error lands under **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — the #433 pathology this PR exists to kill. Mitigations keep this non-blocking: the runner's own `##[error]Process completed with exit code N.` line does **not** match the crap4j detail shape (no `path:digits:`), path-bearing annotations normally use the `::error file=…,line=…::` form (also not matched — `=` not `:`), and the item's message text still names the real path in the foreign table and raw tails. But the fix is the same one-liner class as the previous round — claim the generic shape before the greedy section scanner:

```js
dartAnalyzeViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
dartTestViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
genericErrorViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);   // ← before crap4j
crap4jViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
jscpdViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
```

`::error`/`##[error]` lines never match the crap4j detail shape without the `##[error]path:line:` variant, so no pinned fixture changes (the pathless fallback test stays byte-identical). Alternative: terminate `currentRule` in `crap4jViolations` when a line starts with `##[` or `::` (workflow-command namespace). Please add a regression fixture: a `[FAIL]` header followed by `##[error]<diff-file>:12: msg`, asserting the item's clean path and `ownership === 'owned'`.

---

### Thread 8 — `js/common/ciViolations.js` line 95

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sameFile` suffix matching can over-own when the diff contains a basename-suffix path in a different directory**

`sameFile` treats a violation path as owned when it **ends with** `/<diffPath>`:

```js
return v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d;
```

So a diff containing root-level `x.dart` owns a violation reported as `lib/x.dart` (suffix `/x.dart` matches). Verified against this branch:

```js
tagOwnership([{ path: 'lib/x.dart', ... }], 'diff --git a/x.dart b/x.dart ...')
// → ownership: 'owned'
```

This is deliberate runner-rooted-suffix tolerance (logs like `/home/runner/work/repo/repo/lib/x.dart` must match diff path `lib/x.dart`), and the error direction is fail-safe — an over-owned item is fixed/disputed, never silently dismissed. But with a root file and a same-named nested file both in play, the owned table can name a file the PR only touches elsewhere. Cheap tighten: require the remainder before the suffix to be empty or end at a segment boundary **and** the matched suffix to contain at least one `/` when the violation path has more levels than the diff path — or anchor the suffix match on a full segment list comparison (split both on `/`, compare tails). If the leniency is intentional, a comment stating the trade-off would help the next reader.

---

### Thread 9 — `js/pushReworkChanges.js` line 1990

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runOwnedViolationsGate` accepts `tracker` but never uses it**

```js
function runOwnedViolationsGate(ticketKey, config, scm, tracker, pr, fixSummary) {
```

The `tracker` parameter is dead — the gate reads the snapshot, validates the summary, and reports through `scm` (`postRejectionComment` + `postLapMarker`) only. Every other gate-style helper here (`runLapGate`, `handleReworkBlocked`) uses its tracker for ticket updates; keeping an unused param in the signature invites a future caller to pass a half-built tracker object or wonder whether the gate is supposed to mark the ticket. Drop the parameter (and update the call in `runLapGate` + the AC6b test loaders), or use it to move the ticket to a failed/rework state on rejection if that was the intent.

---

### Thread 10 — `js/pushReworkChanges.js` line 1978

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `handleOwnedViolationsRejected` result omits `blocked: true` — inconsistent with the sibling blocked-path result**

`handleReworkBlocked` returns:

```js
return { success: false, blocked: true, error: 'Rework blocked: no code changes while ...' };
```

while this new failure path returns:

```js
return { success: false, path: 'owned-violations-rejected', ticketKey: ticketKey, error: ... };
```

`runLapGate` wraps both as `{ blocked: true, result }` and the caller just returns `lapGateRun.result`, so behavior is identical today — but any consumer keying on the action result's `blocked` flag (the shape every other failure result in this file carries) sees a different shape for this path. Rework context: extract gate violations (owned vs foreign) to the top of ci_failures.md; forbid dismissing owned violations
## Goal — rework legs see the exact gate violations they must fix (v1)
One sentence: **when a quality gate is red, the rework leg receives every violation line (file:line, rule, measured vs limit) as a first-class, top-of-file list, so that it fixes them instead of declaring the red "not caused by this PR".**

Live: epam/dmtools-dart#433 (gh-409), rework leg run 39308030238 at 2026-10-19 19:05.
- `gate` (crap4dart) failed with:
  ```
  [FAIL] method_size: 1 violations in 5903 methods over their size limits
    test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart:13: main has 100 lines > max 60
  ```
- The file was **added by this PR**. The violation line was present in `ci_failures_full.log`, and inside the last 500 lines of `ci_failures.md`.
- The agent's own grep (`method_size\|> *[0-9]* lines`) matched only the `[FAIL]` header and missed the indented detail line. It concluded *"none of my files exceeds 60 lines… violation is in code the PR does not touch"* and pushed `e20e9665` without fixing it. Its commit even grew the same `main` (+30 lines).
- In the same run a genuinely unrelated red, `agents-gate` (planned-file partition race on agents@main, a dmtools-dart workflow issue), was mixed in. The agent then classified **both** reds as "infra".

## Why this framing
- The fix is not "a smarter model". Context assembly must make violations impossible to miss and must separate PR-owned reds from foreign ones.
- Retracted: the context was missing. It was present but buried: 686-line raw logs × 5 checks, with no structure.

## Architecture
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], assembled by `js/common/githubHelpers.js` (`fetchAndWriteCiFailures` / `buildLogSections`) and `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`.

1. **Violation extractor** (pure function, `js/common/ciViolations.js`), given raw job logs, returns `[{check, rule, path, line, detail}]`. Recognized shapes:
   - crap4dart/crap4j: `[FAIL] <rule>:` header + indented `path:line: …` lines until the next `[PASS|FAIL|WARN]`.
   - dart analyze: `error • … • path:line:col • code`.
   - dart test: `path: <test name> [E]` / `Some tests failed`.
   - jscpd duplication blocks.
   - Generic `##[error]` lines (fallback).
2. **Ownership tag** per violation: `owned` when `path` is in the PR diff (`pr_diff.txt` file list), `foreign` otherwise, and `unknown` when there is no path.
3. `ci_failures.md` starts with a section **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"**, a table of `owned` items. Then "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)". The 500-line tails stay below as evidence.
4. The rework prompt rule is to check `ci_failures.md`: *an owned violation may not be dismissed as unrelated. Fix it or explain, per item, why the gate is wrong.*
5. The post-rework summary must list each owned violation with `fixed` / `disputed: <reason>`. A summary that claims "not caused by this PR" while owned items exist is rejected (the leg is marked failed, and the no-op loop guard counts it).

Invariants:
- I1 — extraction never drops the raw logs. The full log is still written (gh-1045).
- I2 — the extractor is deterministic and covered by unit tests with real log fixtures.
- I3 — an unknown log shape degrades to today's behavior, never to an empty file.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — the #433 gate log fixture yields exactly one owned violation `test/js/require_base_resolution_test.dart:13 method_size main 100>60` (UT-1).
- **AC2** — the #433 agents-gate log yields one `foreign` item (`js/unit-tests/test_recoverDirtyReviewTestCase.js`, not in the diff) (UT-2).
- **AC3** — `ci_failures.md` opens with the owned table, followed by the foreign list (UT-3, snapshot).
- **AC4** — the fixtures for dart analyze, dart test, crap4j and jscpd each produce correct items (UT-4..7).
- **AC5** — unknown shape → no table, the 500-line tail stays as today (REG-1).
- **AC6** — the rework prompt contains the owned-violation rule. A summary validator rejects "unrelated" with owned items open (UT-8).
- **AC7** — replay #433: the rework leg input contains the owned row (IT-1).

## Test plan
`UT` in `js/unit-tests` with fixtures copied from dart run 39301703682 jobs 118246938987 (gate) and 118249670863 (agents-gate). `IT` via the preCliReworkSetup harness. `REG`: existing gh-1045 tests stay green.

### Edge cases
- E1 — violation in a file renamed by the PR → owned (match both old and new paths).
- E2 — more than 50 violations → table capped at 50 with a count, full list in `ci_violations.json`.
- E3 — Windows paths / `./` prefixes are normalized.

## Non-goals
- Fixing the agents-gate race itself (dmtools-dart workflow, separate issue).
- Changing the gate limits.

## PR Description

Closes #1119
### What changed
Rework legs now receive every CI gate violation as a first-class list: a pure extractor (`js/common/ciViolations.js`) parses raw job logs (crap4dart, dart analyze, dart test, jscpd, `##[error]` fallback), tags each item `owned`/`foreign` against the PR diff, and `ci_failures.md` opens with **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** followed by "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)" — the 500-line tails and `ci_failures_full.log` stay below as evidence. The post-rework summary is mechanically validated: a summary dismissing an owned violation as "not caused by this PR"/"unrelated"/"infra" fails the leg and counts as an empty lap.

### Key decisions
- Context assembly, not model judgment: owned rows carry `check | rule | path:line | measured-vs-limit`; the full uncapped list lands in `ci_violations.json` (tables cap at 50 rows)
- Renames count as owned (old+new diff paths); Windows/`./` paths normalized; no diff evidence degrades to `unknown`, never "do not chase"
- Degradation invariant: unknown log shape → no table, `ci_failures.md` assembled exactly as today; raw logs are never dropped
- `preCliReworkSetup` fetches the PR diff **before** CI detection so ownership tagging has it; `preparePRForReview` passes the diff too
- Rejection path (`pushReworkChanges.runOwnedViolationsGate`) posts a per-item rejection comment with the owned table and an empty lap marker for the gh-957 no-op loop guard
- Prompt/instructions updated (`pr_rework_prompt.md`, `instructions/pr_rework/*`, `instructions/review/ci_failures.md`): owned violations must be listed per item with `fixed` / `disputed: <reason>`

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_ciViolations.json   # UT-1..UT-8, E1..E3
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 5015 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LOGS[Failed-check raw logs] --> EX[ciViolations.extractViolations]
  DIFF[pr_diff.txt file list] --> TAG[ciViolations.tagOwnership]
  EX --> TAG
  TAG --> MD["ci_failures.md: owned table → foreign list → raw tails"]
  TAG --> JSON[ci_violations.json uncapped]
  MD --> REWORK[Rework leg fixes owned rows]
  REWORK --> GATE[runOwnedViolationsGate: summary must account fixed/disputed per item]
  GATE -->|dismissal while owned open| FAIL[leg failed + empty lap marker]
  GATE -->|accounted| DONE[normal completion]
```

</details>

```js
dartTestViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
```

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sameFile` suffix matching can over-own when the diff contains a basename-suffix path in a different directory**

`sameFile` treats a violation path as owned when it **ends with** `/<diffPath>`:

```js
return v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d;
```

So a diff containing root-level `x.dart` owns a violation reported as `lib/x.dart` (suffix `/x.dart` matches). Verified against this branch:

```js
// → ownership: 'owned'
```

Cheap tighten: require the remainder before the suffix to be empty or end at a segment boundary **and** the matched suffix to contain at least one `/` when the violation path has more levels than the diff path — or anchor the suffix match on a full segment list comparison (split both on `/`, compare tails). ```

Every other gate-style helper here (`runLapGate`, `handleReworkBlocked`) uses its tracker for ticket updates; keeping an unused param in the signature invites a future caller to pass a half-built tracker object or wonder whether the gate is supposed to mark the ticket. Drop the parameter (and update the call in `runLapGate` + the AC6b test loaders), or use it to move the ticket to a failed/rework state on rejection if that was the intent.

💡 **SUGGESTION (carried over, unchanged from round 2): `sameFile` suffix matching can over-own when the diff contains a basename-suffix path in a different directory**

Still on this head — a violation path is owned when it merely **ends with** `/<diffPath>`:

```js
tagOwnership([{ path: 'lib/x.dart', ... }], 'diff --git a/x.dart b/x.dart ...')
// → 'owned'  (root-level x.dart in the diff owns lib/x.dart)
```

## PR Description

Closes #1119
### What changed
Rework legs now receive every CI gate violation as a first-class list: a pure extractor (`js/common/ciViolations.js`) parses raw job logs (crap4dart, dart analyze, dart test, jscpd, `##[error]` fallback), tags each item `owned`/`foreign` against the PR diff, and `ci_failures.md` opens with **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** followed by "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)" — the 500-line tails and `ci_failures_full.log` stay below as evidence. The post-rework summary is mechanically validated: a summary dismissing an owned violation as "not caused by this PR"/"unrelated"/"infra" fails the leg and counts as an empty lap.

### Key decisions
- Context assembly, not model judgment: owned rows carry `check | rule | path:line | measured-vs-limit`; the full uncapped list lands in `ci_violations.json` (tables cap at 50 rows)
- Renames count as owned (old+new diff paths); Windows/`./` paths normalized; no diff evidence degrades to `unknown`, never "do not chase"
- Degradation invariant: unknown log shape → no table, `ci_failures.md` assembled exactly as today; raw logs are never dropped
- `preCliReworkSetup` fetches the PR diff **before** CI detection so ownership tagging has it; `preparePRForReview` passes the diff too
- Rejection path (`pushReworkChanges.runOwnedViolationsGate`) posts a per-item rejection comment with the owned table and an empty lap marker for the gh-957 no-op loop guard
- Prompt/instructions updated (`pr_rework_prompt.md`, `instructions/pr_rework/*`, `instructions/review/ci_failures.md`): owned violations must be listed per item with `fixed` / `disputed: <reason>`

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_ciViolations.json   # UT-1..UT-8, E1..E3
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 5015 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LOGS[Failed-check raw logs] --> EX[ciViolations.extractViolations]
  DIFF[pr_diff.txt file list] --> TAG[ciViolations.tagOwnership]
  EX --> TAG
  TAG --> MD["ci_failures.md: owned table → foreign list → raw tails"]
  TAG --> JSON[ci_violations.json uncapped]
  MD --> REWORK[Rework leg fixes owned rows]
  REWORK --> GATE[runOwnedViolationsGate: summary must account fixed/disputed per item]
  GATE -->|dismissal while owned open| FAIL[leg failed + empty lap marker]
  GATE -->|accounted| DONE[normal completion]
```

</details>

### Thread 7 — `js/common/ciViolations.js` line 372

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: residual parser-order contamination — a path-bearing `##[error]path:line:` line inside an unterminated `[FAIL]` section is still swallowed with a mangled path and rendered as "foreign, do not chase"**

The reorder in `extractViolations` (this head) fully fixes the reported dart-analyze/dart-test contamination — I verified the `gate_plus_analyze.log` repro now extracts the bullet with its clean path and tags it `owned` (control check below). One narrower shape of the same family remains: `genericErrorViolations` runs **last**, so a `##[error]` line whose message carries `path:line:` and that appears **after a `[FAIL] <rule>:` header with no intervening `[PASS]/[WARN]/[FAIL]` marker** is claimed by `crap4jViolations` first.

Reproduced against this branch's module (`js/common/ciViolations.js`):

```js
extractViolations(
  '[FAIL] method_size: 1 violations\n' +
  ' a/one.dart:1: too big\n' +
  '##[error]lib/widgets/foo.dart:12: build failed', 'gate')
// → [
//   { rule:'method_size', path:'a/one.dart', line:1 },                              // correct
//   { rule:'method_size', path:'##[error]lib/widgets/foo.dart', line:12, ... }      // mangled
// ]
```

The mangled path (`##[error]` prefix baked into the captured "path") fails the `sameFile` suffix check even when `lib/widgets/foo.dart` IS in the diff, so a genuinely owned error lands under **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — the #433 pathology this PR exists to kill. Mitigations keep this non-blocking: the runner's own `##[error]Process completed with exit code N.` line does **not** match the crap4j detail shape (no `path:digits:`), path-bearing annotations normally use the `::error file=…,line=…::` form (also not matched — `=` not `:`), and the item's message text still names the real path in the foreign table and raw tails. But the fix is the same one-liner class as the previous round — claim the generic shape before the greedy section scanner:

```js
dartAnalyzeViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
dartTestViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
genericErrorViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);   // ← before crap4j
crap4jViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
jscpdViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
```

`::error`/`##[error]` lines never match the crap4j detail shape without the `##[error]path:line:` variant, so no pinned fixture changes (the pathless fallback test stays byte-identical). Alternative: terminate `currentRule` in `crap4jViolations` when a line starts with `##[` or `::` (workflow-command namespace). Please add a regression fixture: a `[FAIL]` header followed by `##[error]<diff-file>:12: msg`, asserting the item's clean path and `ownership === 'owned'`.

---

### Thread 8 — `js/common/ciViolations.js` line 95

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sameFile` suffix matching can over-own when the diff contains a basename-suffix path in a different directory**

`sameFile` treats a violation path as owned when it **ends with** `/<diffPath>`:

```js
return v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d;
```

So a diff containing root-level `x.dart` owns a violation reported as `lib/x.dart` (suffix `/x.dart` matches). Verified against this branch:

```js
tagOwnership([{ path: 'lib/x.dart', ... }], 'diff --git a/x.dart b/x.dart ...')
// → ownership: 'owned'
```

This is deliberate runner-rooted-suffix tolerance (logs like `/home/runner/work/repo/repo/lib/x.dart` must match diff path `lib/x.dart`), and the error direction is fail-safe — an over-owned item is fixed/disputed, never silently dismissed. But with a root file and a same-named nested file both in play, the owned table can name a file the PR only touches elsewhere. Cheap tighten: require the remainder before the suffix to be empty or end at a segment boundary **and** the matched suffix to contain at least one `/` when the violation path has more levels than the diff path — or anchor the suffix match on a full segment list comparison (split both on `/`, compare tails). If the leniency is intentional, a comment stating the trade-off would help the next reader.

---

### Thread 9 — `js/pushReworkChanges.js` line 1990

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runOwnedViolationsGate` accepts `tracker` but never uses it**

```js
function runOwnedViolationsGate(ticketKey, config, scm, tracker, pr, fixSummary) {
```

The `tracker` parameter is dead — the gate reads the snapshot, validates the summary, and reports through `scm` (`postRejectionComment` + `postLapMarker`) only. Every other gate-style helper here (`runLapGate`, `handleReworkBlocked`) uses its tracker for ticket updates; keeping an unused param in the signature invites a future caller to pass a half-built tracker object or wonder whether the gate is supposed to mark the ticket. Drop the parameter (and update the call in `runLapGate` + the AC6b test loaders), or use it to move the ticket to a failed/rework state on rejection if that was the intent.

---

### Thread 10 — `js/pushReworkChanges.js` line 1978

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `handleOwnedViolationsRejected` result omits `blocked: true` — inconsistent with the sibling blocked-path result**

`handleReworkBlocked` returns:

```js
return { success: false, blocked: true, error: 'Rework blocked: no code changes while ...' };
```

while this new failure path returns:

```js
return { success: false, path: 'owned-violations-rejected', ticketKey: ticketKey, error: ... };
```

`runLapGate` wraps both as `{ blocked: true, result }` and the caller just returns `lapGateRun.result`, so behavior is identical today — but any consumer keying on the action result's `blocked` flag (the shape every other failure result in this file carries) sees a different shape for this path. Add `blocked: true` for consistency, or note on the `path` field that it is the machine-readable discriminator.

- **PR #**: 1131
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1131
- **Title**: gh-1119 Rework context: extract gate violations (owned vs foreign) to the top of ci_failures.md forbid dismissing owned violations
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1119` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 29
- **Additions**: +2086
- **Deletions**: -36
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T21:45:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T01:32:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1119
### What changed
Rework legs now receive every CI gate violation as a first-class list: a pure extractor (`js/common/ciViolations.js`) parses raw job logs (crap4dart, dart analyze, dart test, jscpd, `##[error]` fallback), tags each item `owned`/`foreign` against the PR diff, and `ci_failures.md` opens with **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** followed by "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)" — the 500-line tails and `ci_failures_full.log` stay below as evidence. The post-rework summary is mechanically validated: a summary dismissing an owned violation as "not caused by this PR"/"unrelated"/"infra" fails the leg and counts as an empty lap.

### Key decisions
- Context assembly, not model judgment: owned rows carry `check | rule | path:line | measured-vs-limit`; the full uncapped list lands in `ci_violations.json` (tables cap at 50 rows)
- Renames count as owned (old+new diff paths); Windows/`./` paths normalized; no diff evidence degrades to `unknown`, never "do not chase"
- Degradation invariant: unknown log shape → no table, `ci_failures.md` assembled exactly as today; raw logs are never dropped
- `preCliReworkSetup` fetches the PR diff **before** CI detection so ownership tagging has it; `preparePRForReview` passes the diff too
- Rejection path (`pushReworkChanges.runOwnedViolationsGate`) posts a per-item rejection comment with the owned table and an empty lap marker for the gh-957 no-op loop guard
- Prompt/instructions updated (`pr_rework_prompt.md`, `instructions/pr_rework/*`, `instructions/review/ci_failures.md`): owned violations must be listed per item with `fixed` / `disputed: <reason>`

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_ciViolations.json   # UT-1..UT-8, E1..E3
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 5015 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LOGS[Failed-check raw logs] --> EX[ciViolations.extractViolations]
  DIFF[pr_diff.txt file list] --> TAG[ciViolations.tagOwnership]
  EX --> TAG
  TAG --> MD["ci_failures.md: owned table → foreign list → raw tails"]
  TAG --> JSON[ci_violations.json uncapped]
  MD --> REWORK[Rework leg fixes owned rows]
  REWORK --> GATE[runOwnedViolationsGate: summary must account fixed/disputed per item]
  GATE -->|dismissal while owned open| FAIL[leg failed + empty lap marker]
  GATE -->|accounted| DONE[normal completion]
```

</details>

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: residual parser-order contamination — a path-bearing `##[error]path:line:` line inside an unterminated `[FAIL]` section is still swallowed with a mangled path and rendered as "foreign, do not chase"**

The reorder in `extractViolations` (this head) fully fixes the reported dart-analyze/dart-test contamination — I verified the `gate_plus_analyze.log` repro now extracts the bullet with its clean path and tags it `owned` (control check below). One narrower shape of the same family remains: `genericErrorViolations` runs **last**, so a `##[error]` line whose message carries `path:line:` and that appears **after a `[FAIL] <rule>:` header with no intervening `[PASS]/[WARN]/[FAIL]` marker** is claimed by `crap4jViolations` first.

Reproduced against this branch's module (`js/common/ciViolations.js`):

```js
extractViolations(
  '[FAIL] method_size: 1 violations\n' +
  ' a/one.dart:1: too big\n' +
  '##[error]lib/widgets/foo.dart:12: build failed', 'gate')

//   { rule:'method_size', path:'a/one.dart', line:1 },                              // correct
//   { rule:'method_size', path:'##[error]lib/widgets/foo.dart', line:12, ... }      // mangled
// ]
```

The mangled path (`##[error]` prefix baked into the captured "path") fails the `sameFile` suffix check even when `lib/widgets/foo.dart` IS in the diff, so a genuinely owned error lands under **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — the #433 pathology this PR exists to kill. Mitigations keep this non-blocking: the runner's own `##[error]Process completed with exit code N.` line does **not** match the crap4j detail shape (no `path:digits:`), path-bearing annotations normally use the `::error file=…,line=…::` form (also not matched — `=` not `:`), and the item's message text still names the real path in the foreign table and raw tails. But the fix is the same one-liner class as the previous round — claim the generic shape before the greedy section scanner:

```js
dartAnalyzeViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
dartTestViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
genericErrorViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);   // ← before crap4j
crap4jViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
jscpdViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
```

`::error`/`##[error]` lines never match the crap4j detail shape without the `##[error]path:line:` variant, so no pinned fixture changes (the pathless fallback test stays byte-identical). Alternative: terminate `currentRule` in `crap4jViolations` when a line starts with `##[` or `::` (workflow-command namespace). Please add a regression fixture: a `[FAIL]` header followed by `##[error]<diff-file>:12: msg`, asserting the item's clean path and `ownership === 'owned'`.

---

### Thread 8 — `js/common/ciViolations.js` line 95

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sameFile` suffix matching can over-own when the diff contains a basename-suffix path in a different directory**

`sameFile` treats a violation path as owned when it **ends with** `/<diffPath>`:

```js
return v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d;
```

So a diff containing root-level `x.dart` owns a violation reported as `lib/x.dart` (suffix `/x.dart` matches). Verified against this branch:

```js
tagOwnership([{ path: 'lib/x.dart', ... }], 'diff --git a/x.dart b/x.dart ...')
// → ownership: 'owned'
```

This is deliberate runner-rooted-suffix tolerance (logs like `/home/runner/work/repo/repo/lib/x.dart` must match diff path `lib/x.dart`), and the error direction is fail-safe — an over-owned item is fixed/disputed, never silently dismissed. But with a root file and a same-named nested file both in play, the owned table can name a file the PR only touches elsewhere. Cheap tighten: require the remainder before the suffix to be empty or end at a segment boundary **and** the matched suffix to contain at least one `/` when the violation path has more levels than the diff path — or anchor the suffix match on a full segment list comparison (split both on `/`, compare tails). If the leniency is intentional, a comment stating the trade-off would help the next reader.

---

### Thread 9 — `js/pushReworkChanges.js` line 1990

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runOwnedViolationsGate` accepts `tracker` but never uses it**

```js
function runOwnedViolationsGate(ticketKey, config, scm, tracker, pr, fixSummary) {
```

The `tracker` parameter is dead — the gate reads the snapshot, validates the summary, and reports through `scm` (`postRejectionComment` + `postLapMarker`) only. Every other gate-style helper here (`runLapGate`, `handleReworkBlocked`) uses its tracker for ticket updates; keeping an unused param in the signature invites a future caller to pass a half-built tracker object or wonder whether the gate is supposed to mark the ticket. Drop the parameter (and update the call in `runLapGate` + the AC6b test loaders), or use it to move the ticket to a failed/rework state on rejection if that was the intent.

---

### Thread 10 — `js/pushReworkChanges.js` line 1978

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `handleOwnedViolationsRejected` result omits `blocked: true` — inconsistent with the sibling blocked-path result**

`handleReworkBlocked` returns:

```js
return { success: false, blocked: true, error: 'Rework blocked: no code changes while ...' };
```

while this new failure path returns:

```js
return { success: false, path: 'owned-violations-rejected', ticketKey: ticketKey, error: ... };
```

`runLapGate` wraps both as `{ blocked: true, result }` and the caller just returns `lapGateRun.result`, so behavior is identical today — but any consumer keying on the action result's `blocked` flag (the shape every other failure result in this file carries) sees a different shape for this path. Rework legs now receive every CI gate violation as a first-class list: a pure extractor (`js/common/ciViolations.js`) parses raw job logs (crap4dart, dart analyze, dart test, jscpd, `##[error]` fallback), tags each item `owned`/`foreign` against the PR diff, and `ci_failures.md` opens with **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** followed by "Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)" — the 500-line tails and `ci_failures_full.log` stay below as evidence. **dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):

The reorder in `extractViolations` (this head) fully fixes the reported dart-analyze/dart-test contamination — I verified the `gate_plus_analyze.log` repro now extracts the bullet with its clean path and tags it `owned` (control check below). One narrower shape of the same family remains: `genericErrorViolations` runs **last**, so a `##[error]` line whose message carries `path:line:` and that appears **after a `[FAIL] <rule>:` header with no intervening `[PASS]/[WARN]/[FAIL]` marker** is claimed by `crap4jViolations` first.

Reproduced against this branch's module (`js/common/ciViolations.js`):

```js
extractViolations(
  '[FAIL] method_size: 1 violations\n' +
  ' a/one.dart:1: too big\n' +
  '##[error]lib/widgets/foo.dart:12: build failed', 'gate')
// → [
//   { rule:'method_size', path:'a/one.dart', line:1 },                              // correct
//   { rule:'method_size', path:'##[error]lib/widgets/foo.dart', line:12, ... }      // mangled
// ]
```

The mangled path (`##[error]` prefix baked into the captured "path") fails the `sameFile` suffix check even when `lib/widgets/foo.dart` IS in the diff, so a genuinely owned error lands under **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — the #433 pathology this PR exists to kill. Mitigations keep this non-blocking: the runner's own `##[error]Process completed with exit code N.` line does **not** match the crap4j detail shape (no `path:digits:`), path-bearing annotations normally use the `::error file=…,line=…::` form (also not matched — `=` not `:`), and the item's message text still names the real path in the foreign table and raw tails. But the fix is the same one-liner class as the previous round — claim the generic shape before the greedy section scanner:

```js
dartAnalyzeViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
dartTestViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
genericErrorViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);   // ← before crap4j
crap4jViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
jscpdViolations(lines, checkName, taken, out);
```

`::error`/`##[error]` lines never match the crap4j detail shape without the `##[error]path:line:` variant, so no pinned fixture changes (the pathless fallback test stays byte-identical). Alternative: terminate `currentRule` in `crap4jViolations` when a line starts with `##[` or `::` (workflow-command namespace). Please add a regression fixture: a `[FAIL]` header followed by `##[error]<diff-file>:12: msg`, asserting the item's clean path and `ownership === 'owned'`.

### Thread 8 — `js/common/ciViolations.js` line 95

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sameFile` suffix matching can over-own when the diff contains a basename-suffix path in a different directory**

`sameFile` treats a violation path as owned when it **ends with** `/<diffPath>`:

```js
return v.length > d.length + 1 && v.substring(v.length - d.length - 1) === '/' + d;
```

So a diff containing root-level `x.dart` owns a violation reported as `lib/x.dart` (suffix `/x.dart` matches). Verified against this branch:

```js
tagOwnership([{ path: 'lib/x.dart', ... }], 'diff --git a/x.dart b/x.dart ...')
// → ownership: 'owned'
```

This is deliberate runner-rooted-suffix tolerance (logs like `/home/runner/work/repo/repo/lib/x.dart` must match diff path `lib/x.dart`), and the error direction is fail-safe — an over-owned item is fixed/disputed, never silently dismissed. But with a root file and a same-named nested file both in play, the owned table can name a file the PR only touches elsewhere. Cheap tighten: require the remainder before the suffix to be empty or end at a segment boundary **and** the matched suffix to contain at least one `/` when the violation path has more levels than the diff path — or anchor the suffix match on a full segment list comparison (split both on `/`, compare tails). If the leniency is intentional, a comment stating the trade-off would help the next reader.

The `tracker` parameter is dead — the gate reads the snapshot, validates the summary, and reports through `scm` (`postRejectionComment` + `postLapMarker`) only. Every other gate-style helper here (`runLapGate`, `handleReworkBlocked`) uses its tracker for ticket updates; keeping an unused param in the signature invites a future caller to pass a half-built tracker object or wonder whether the gate is supposed to mark the ticket.
